short.en: Give every GLPI entity its own login page, showing only that entity's SSO providers.

long.en:
## Entity Login Portals
When several organisations share one GLPI, every SSO button appears on the same login page: ten organisations means ten buttons, and every user sees all of them.
This plugin gives each entity its own login page, reached by a slug:
- `https://glpi.example.com/` — the login form, with **no** SSO buttons - `https://glpi.example.com/acme` — the login form plus **only** Acme's SSO - `https://glpi.example.com/globex` — the login form plus **only** Globex's SSO
### How it works
Supported SSO plugins list every configured provider globally, with no entity awareness. This plugin takes over the button rendering and scopes the list to the portal being visited, emitting markup that keeps each SSO plugin's own contract — so the authentication flows themselves are completely untouched.
**GLPI core is not modified, and neither is any SSO plugin.** Their tables are only ever read. Deactivating this plugin instantly restores the original behaviour; uninstalling drops only this plugin's two tables.
### Supported SSO plugins
- **samlSSO** (`samlsso`) — SAML 2.0 - **Single Sign-On** (`singlesignon`) — OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect
Providers from both can be mixed on a single portal. At least one of them must be installed for the plugin to be useful.
### Short URLs
GLPI serves plugin routes under `/plugins/<key>/`, so portals work out of the box at `/plugins/entitylogin/portal/<slug>`. The short `/acme` form is produced by a one-line rewrite on your reverse proxy; ready-made recipes for **nginx**, **Traefik** and **Caddy** are in the README.
### Requirements
- GLPI 11.0.x - One of the supported SSO plugins
### Scope
A portal controls which SSO buttons are *displayed*. It is a presentation boundary, not an access-control boundary: login behaviour itself is unchanged, so any valid user can still sign in from any portal page.
